summary: Discovery call to qualify SageBridge's embedding+rerank use case. Focus on throughput, embedding dimensionality, hybrid search (BM25 + vector), and hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Customer leans toward a Dedicated pilot but has strict compliance and VPC needs for production. They asked about fallback strategies, KV cache warmup, quantized embeddings, and vector DB interoperability.

pilot success criteria and next steps
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-18 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ivy Morales (Redwood AE), Kenji Tanaka (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (SageBridge Head of Search), Marcus Lee (ML Infra), Dana Ortiz (Product), Sam (Eng)

00:00 - Ivy: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll give like a quick agenda then jump into your current stack and requirements. do you want to kick off, priya?
00:14 - Priya: yeah thanks ivy. so quick context, we're building a customer insights search that merges BM25 signals with embeddings for rerank. currently using an open source vector DB and FAISS offline, redis for short term caching. our main pain is throughput during spikes and the rerank cost is getting expensive, also latency tail occasionally spikes to 400-600ms which hurts product.
00:38 - Marcus: to add, infra is kubernetes on AWS, we have VPC restrictions and need audit logs. we prefer not to send PII outside our VPC for production.
00:50 - Ivy: got it, thanks. so two things we'd want to qualify: what pilot looks like and hosting options. kenji can you run through how redwood handles embeddings+rerank?
01:05 - Kenji: sure. high level, we support hybrid pipelines — embed retrieval then rerank with a generation or small ranker. on hosting: hosted API is fastest to get started, dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictability, and private gives you a control plane in your VPC. from a perf side we do continuous batching, kv cache for prefix re-use, and support quantized kernels which reduces memory for embedding throughput.
01:32 - Sam: when you say kv cache is that for the LM cache or embeddings?
01:37 - Kenji: primarly for autoregressive models' KV cache. for embeddings we have prefix caching and result-level caching. for rerank specifically we recommend precomputing embeddings for doc corpus and using a vector DB for fast fanout, then call the ranker on a small top-k set.
02:00 - Dana: our dataset is 75M docs, avg doc text 1.2 KB, roughly 30 shards in our vector DB. embeddings are currently 4k dim (we swapped from 1k earlier). is 4k standard? cost is huge.
02:17 - Kenji: 4k is high. many teams use 1k-2k for semantic search; 4k helps with some precision but increases index size and retrieval cost. quantization and sparse/compact embeddings are options — Redwood Optimize will suggest tradeoffs but for throughput, smaller dims plus a strong reranker often wins.
02:40 - Priya: what's the impact on latency if we run rerank remotely vs inside our VPC? we worry about cross-VPC hops.
02:48 - Ivy: that's one reason teams pick Dedicated or Private. Dedicated keeps the data plane in cloud region controlled by Redwood but isolated; Private/VPC lets you keep traffic within your network. remote hosted will add network egress and potential extra latency.
03:05 - Marcus: compliance wise we need SOC2 + customer-managed KMS for keys. do you support HSM?
03:12 - Kenji: yes we integrate with customer KMS providers and HSMs for private deployments. audit logs and RBAC are available. for Hosted we have SOC2 but if you need customer KMS and full network isolation Private is the option.
03:30 - Ivy: would you be open to a Dedicated pilot first to validate perf and then migrate to Private?
03:36 - Priya: yes possibly. budget approval might prefer dedicated commit vs building private right away.
03:44 - Kenji: couple of questions on traffic shape — what QPS and tail latency SLO do you target for the reranker?
03:52 - Marcus: peak QPS ~350 qps for retrieval calls, rerank only for top-50 candidate set on 5% of queries, so effective rerank QPS ~17-20 QPS but those calls are heavier. SLO goal p50 80ms, p95 220ms. tail performance is the blocker.
04:17 - Kenji: that helps. for rerank we often suggest keeping top-k small (16-50) and using batching on the GPU side; continuous batching reduces token overhead. also fallback to a smaller model when load spikes keeps latency stable.
04:36 - Priya: fallback models — are those auto-triggered? how do you pick?
04:41 - Kenji: you can configure policies: latency-based fallback or queue-depth triggers. we also support auto-rollbacks and can route to a lower-cost variant.
04:52 - Dana: on vector DB integration, does Redwood push to your DB or do you pull?
04:56 - Ivy: both patterns exist. common is Redwood makes vector query calls to your DB (we support Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate and general FAISS endpoints) and we can also host a managed index if needed. integration is via connectors and SDKs.
05:15 - Marcus: our sharding is manual in our DB, we worry about fanout and cross-shard latency. can Redwood handle async fanout and merge?
05:24 - Kenji: we do fanout strategies: fanout client-side vs server-side, and we can parallelize queries across shards. for very large indices we recommend routing policies or shard-awareness to reduce cross-shard traffic. there's also a cache layer to reduce repeated lookups for hot docs.
05:42 - Priya: curious on quantized embeddings — are they lossy? will we lose recall?
05:47 - Kenji: quantization trades size for some precision. with good calibration you can get near-original recall, especially if rerank reruns a higher fidelity model on the shortlist. we also support multi-tier indices: a compact index for fanout then exact embed re-ranking.
06:10 - Sam: our devs want to run a smoke test with 10k queries and measure p95. can you provide a benchmark harness?
06:18 - Ivy: yes kenji will share a benchmark template. kenji: is there anything we need from them to run an initial sketch?
06:23 - Kenji: sample index stats (docs, dims, shard count), a small query corpus (1k-10k) and the rerank prompt/templates. ideal if you can expose a staging endpoint or we can run against a snapshot.
06:38 - Priya: ok we'll prepare 1k queries and the index metrics.
06:42 - Dana: what's the expected cost delta between hosting models on Dedicated vs Hosted for our scale?
06:47 - Ivy: depends on commit. Dedicated has upfront commitment but predictable per-token/per-hour cost and better SLOs. Hosted pays as-you-go and is easier to start. we'll send a TCO worksheet with sample numbers.
07:02 - Marcus: do you support model quantization at the transformer-kernel level on dedicated GPUs?
07:08 - Kenji: yes, our runtime picks optimized kernels and supports int8/4 quantization paths when model architecture and accuracy permit. we also do memory planning to maximize batch size without blowing up latency.
07:20 - Priya: any concerns about vacuuming or index staleness with caching? our index updates hourly.
07:26 - Kenji: prefix/result caching TTLs can be tuned; for hourly updates we recommend invalidation hooks from your pipeline to Redwood or short TTLs. for embeddings, we typically rely on reindex triggers.
07:40 - Ivy: quick qual question: who owns the vector DB in prod? you or us?
07:44 - Priya: we own it in prod for now. we might want Redwood-managed index later but currently our security policy prefers customer-owned index.
07:53 - Kenji: ok that sets the integration pattern. we'll assume you have a vector DB behind VPC. for pilot, a common pattern is Dedicated with VPC peering and limited access.
08:05 - Sam: how do you handle secrets and KMS for model keys and embedding keys?
08:10 - Kenji: on Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; on Dedicated you can bring your own KMS depending on plan. Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default.
08:22 - Dana: tell me more about the canary/rollout and monitoring for regressions in relevance — do you support evaluation hooks?
08:30 - Ivy: yes we have Redwood Optimize which can run evals on prompt sets, track quality regressions and alert on drifts tied to a prompt set. rollouts can be canaryed by percent and we support automatic rollback if quality drops.
08:45 - Priya: nice. for pilot success criteria we want: rerank p95 under 250ms for top-50, retrieval recall lift 8-12% over BM25 baseline, and operational docs for compliance.
09:00 - Ivy: that's helpful — we'll map the pilot to those metrics.
09:05 - Marcus: one last question about cost-saving techniques: prefix caching, batching, and using smaller rerank models — anything else?
09:13 - Kenji: also model sharding, model distillation, and quantized embeddings. you can also do cascade rerank where a cheaper ranker filters then a heavier model scores top results.
09:28 - Priya: timeline wise, procurement says 6 week pilot ideally. are you able to commit?
09:33 - Ivy: yes that's reasonable. we'll send SOW draft and pricing.
09:37 - Dana: okay great. next steps?
09:40 - Ivy: recap: Ivy sends pricing/TCO and SOW draft, Kenji sends benchmark template and runs a quick sketch once you send index metrics, SageBridge provides 1k queries and index stats. schedule technical deep dive next Thursday.
09:54 - Priya: sounds good thanks everyone.
10:00 - Ivy: thanks all.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-heard words — e.g., "vacuuming" may have been "vacuumming" in capture. there are crosstalk moments. end of transcript.
